newsitem.title: USA: Intel unveils new computer chip amid flaw report.
newsitem.headline: Intel unveils new computer chip amid flaw report.

text.p: Intel Corp. on Wednesday released its Pentium II computer chips, which set a new speed record and include advanced multimedia capabilities, but a possible flaw in the devices took some of the zip out of the launch.

More than 100 computer makers will introduce personal computers designed around the Pentium II, including computer giant International Business Machines Corp., Compaq Computer Corp., the world's biggest PC maker; Dell Computer Corp; and Gateway 2000 Inc., Intel said.

The fastest of Intel's new family of microprocessors -- the heart of the PC -- runs at a speed of 300 megahertz, and will sell for $1,981, the company said. Previously, the fastest chips offered by the world's biggest semiconductor maker ran at 200 megahertz.
Intel will also offer 266-megahertz chips priced at $775 and 233-megahertz for $636. Pricing is in 1,000-unit lots.

The Santa Clara, Calif.-based company said it is still running tests to determine whether the chip has a flaw. Earlier this week, an engineer posted a report on a Web site on the Internet that the chip makes computational errors in some rare cases.

"I think it's premature to hazard a guess," Paul Otellini, executive vice president at Intel, said when asked about how severe the possible flaw could be. "We heard about it in terms of the posting (on the Web)."
Otellini said Intel is continuing to test the chip and should have more information by the end of the week.
The report of the flaw, which received wide attention, said it involved so-called floating point calculations.
In 1994, a floating point glitch in Intel's original Pentium chip cost the company $475 million.
The company initially tried to minimise the seriousness of the flaw, but in the end established a huge programme to replace the chip for virtually any customer who requested one.
